method.design: Matched pair on identical query. Treatment = client's authenticated Chrome (Genius Level 2). Control = separate DevTools-driven Chrome instance, signed out, no extensions installed.
method.controlled_for: same destination, dates, occupancy, market, and day of capture
method.why_this_matters: Personalisation claims are normally asserted from one session. This isolates what membership actually changes.

finding_F11.claim: Loyalty membership changes the ranking surface by exactly one axis, and that axis is another PRICE axis.
finding_F11.evidence: Signed out: 10 sort options, no Genius entry. Signed in at Genius Level 2: the same 10 plus 'Genius discounts first'. Result count and ranking disclosure identical.
finding_F11.why_it_matters: Reinforces F-09 from the other direction. Booking.com's loyalty programme does not unlock an ease, effort or confidence axis — it unlocks a further discount axis. Across both states, zero of 11 axes concern how easy a trip will be.

finding_F12.claim: Booking.com fires a Google One Tap sign-in prompt at a signed-out user during search.
finding_F12.evidence: Navigating the signed-out instance to the search results URL opened a Google accounts sign-in page as a second tab.
finding_F12.note: Not interacted with. No credentials were entered at any point in this research.

capability_split.clients_chrome_via_extension: authenticated, personalised, BUT carries third-party extensions (Directo, vio) that inject UI, and exposes no network-protocol inspection
capability_split.devtools_instance: signed out and extension-clean, WITH network inspection, accessibility snapshots and device emulation

method_note_for_remaining_13.consequence: Run both per competitor. The signed-out clean instance is the control and the source of any screenshot-derived claim; the authenticated instance supplies personalised and post-purchase surfaces. Contamination and personalisation stop being confounded.

not_observed: whether prices themselves differ between the two states (compared sort surface only, not price values)
whether result ORDER differs under an identical sort selection
logged-in-only surfaces beyond the sort list
